content.text: On accuracy, the evidence is mixed. Bonilla López et al. (2018) found that metalinguistic codes were effective for enhancing learners' immediate grammatical and non-grammatical accuracy during text revision. Liu and Wu (2019) found that students favoured direct correction in conjunction with metalinguistic explanations (215/447, 48.10%), followed by direct correction without metalinguistic explanations (111/447, 24.83%). Razmi and Ghane (2024) reported that direct unfocused WCF improved writing performance (d = 1.32), but their design did not provide revision opportunities, and the authors speculated that engaging learners in revision can boost the effect of direct WCF.

citationLinks.sentence: On engagement, Bonilla López et al. (2018) found that a mental-effort measure of cognitive load was significantly lower when learners processed direct corrections targeting grammatical issues, implying that metalinguistic codes impose greater processing demands.
